result.title: Divergent Paths: Learning an Outcome-Predictive Representation of LLM Agent Trajectories
result.summary: In this work, we reframe agentic trajectories as paths through a shared embedding space of actions and environmental observations. We show that successful and failed rollouts of the same task separate in this space, with simple per-task discriminators predicting held-out rollout outcomes at up to 0.95 AUROC across three agent benchmarks and three policy models. To exploit this signal across tasks, we introduce Precog-RM, a transformer-based model that meta-learns a representation in which outcome prediction can be performed in a few-shot setting. We show that Precog-RM generalizes to unseen tasks and models, and gives confident predictions of trajectory success long before termination. Deployed as an early stopping controller for Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) on Tau2-Bench, Precog-RM cuts training FLOPs by up to 47.3\% while maintaining performance comparable to baseline GRPO.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将 LLM agent 轨迹视为动作与环境观测共享嵌入空间中的路径，用逐任务判别器及元学习的 Precog-RM 在终止前预测 rollout 成败，并作为 GRPO 的早停控制器把训练 FLOPs 降低最多 47.3%。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「由潜在轨迹表示预测结果并据此提前终止」的机制，可能为 LVR 的 STOP 决策与推理成本—收益权衡、轨迹监督提供可核查线索，但研究对象是文本 agent 轨迹而非视觉推理状态，迁移需验证。
